blocks.text: Screening at cinemas around the UK – find out more .
Screenwriters Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi, Alberto Conejero
With Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Penélope Cruz

Spain, 1932. A young man awaits to see if he has secured membership of the local casino. In 1937, a young nationalist soldier guards a republican prisoner. Jump to 2017 and an unexpected document is inherited by an historian from his grandfather. These timelines and a breathtaking cinematic audacity shapes this dazzlingly constructed and performed triptych about communication, inheritance, silence and memory.
Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury and nudity.
Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .
For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.
If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

blocks.text: Set against a backdrop of widening class divisions and capitalist excess, Florian Zeller’s elegantly crafted psychological thriller is anchored by magnificent performances from Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.
Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s intense psychological study, featuring extraordinary performances by Javier Bardem and Victoria Luengo, explores the limits of power and control.
Ira Sachs cements his position as one of the great chroniclers of New York life with this tender, earthy portrait of the city’s gay scene in the 1980s.
